title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the Teichmüller notes Grothendieck attaches to an oriented polygon P a Riemann surface Sigma_P, which is the 'double' of P. It carries an antiholomorphic involution tau and a holomorphic action of the dihedral symmetry group D_P. He wants to identify the group Pi_P^D, written on p.85 as an amalgam D(rho) *_{D_1} D(sigma_a), with the orbifold ('mixed', 'with signature') fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} with signature infinity·(0) + 2·(1) + n·(infinity). The previous page's margin calls the a-priori route 'un peu une tricherie' (a bit of a cheat), because one must first exhibit Sigma_P explicitly as a pull-back of the universal map. This page supplies that, in the pinned ('épinglé') case.

(91) The standard model.
- P_0 is the regular polygon with vertices S_0 = mu_n(C), joined by arcs of the unit circle U.
- Sigma_P = P^1(C), the Riemann sphere.
- D_P^+ = mu_n acts by rotations z -> zeta z.
- tau(z) = 1/conj(z) is the reflection in U.

The tower of maps.
- The universal map (carte universelle) X_0 is {0} ⊂ [0,1] ⊂ P^1: vertex at 0, edge midpoint at 1, face centre at infinity.
- The cyclotomic map of order 1, X_1, is the pull-back of X_0 by f(z) = -(z-1)^2/(4z). It has one vertex z=1, one edge whose midpoint is z=-1, and two monogon faces with centres 0 and infinity.
- The cyclotomic map X_n is the pull-back of X_1 by z -> z^n.
- The composite is (92): g_n(z) = -(z^n-1)^2/(4z^n), of degree 2n.

Fibres of g_n.
- Over 0: the n-th roots of unity, each with ramification 2. These are the vertices, of valency 2.
- Over 1: the solutions of (z^n+1)^2 = 0, i.e. z^n = -1, each with ramification 2. These are the edge midpoints.
- Over infinity: the points 0 and infinity, each with ramification n. These are the centres of the two n-gon faces.

Galois structure.
- g_n is invariant under z -> zeta z and under z -> 1/z, which together generate a dihedral group of order 2n = deg g_n.
- So X_n -> X_0 is Galois with group D_n = D_{P_0}, branched only over 0, 1, infinity with indices 2, 2, n.
- Removing the vertices, X_n^* = Sigma_{P_0}^* is a finite Galois cover of X_0 minus {0}, branched only at 1 and infinity with indices 2 and n.

Purpose. On the next page this gives canonical (at first only outer) isomorphisms between pi_1 of X_n^* and the orbifold group pi_1(P^1; infinity·0 + 2·1 + n·infinity) ≅ Z/2 * Z/n. These are then rigidified by choosing base points: the flag (repère) r_0 = (R_0, Q_{a_0}, P_omega) and the 'north pole' P_+ = exp(2 i pi/6) of X_0^+.
errors: No mathematical errors. f(z) = -(z-1)^2/(4z) indeed sends 1 to 0 doubly and -1 to 1 doubly, with simple poles at 0 and infinity. g_n is invariant under z -> 1/z. The ramification data 2, 2, n are correct.

Minor ambiguity: D_P^+ = mu_n denotes the rotation subgroup. The full group D_P acting holomorphically on Sigma_P also contains z -> 1/z, which is the polygon reflection z -> conj(z) composed with tau. This is implicit in the text rather than stated.

ideas.what: Regular polygon / cyclotomic map X_n on the Riemann sphere as pull-back of the universal map by the Belyi function g_n(z) = -(z^n-1)^2/(4z^n), giving a dihedral Galois cover with branching (2,2,n)
ideas.modern_name: Regular dihedral dessin d'enfant (the 'n-gon on the equator'); its Belyi function
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard example in dessins d'enfants theory (Grothendieck's school; Jones–Singerman 1978 on maps and triangle groups; Lando–Zvonkin's book)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses maps as covers of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} and the cartographic group, but not this explicit formula as far as known

ideas.what: Double Sigma_P of a polygon, with antiholomorphic involution tau and dihedral group action; the quotient is P^1 with signature infinity·0 + 2·1 + n·infinity
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold double / Schwarz reflection principle; triangle-group quotient (infinity, 2, n), which for n = 3 gives PSL(2,Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Klein); orbifold language due to Thurston
ideas.where_published: Related material in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, reflections, 'mixed' fundamental groups)

ideas.what: Comparison of pi_1 of the Galois cover minus the vertices with the orbifold fundamental group with signature, as outer isomorphisms rigidified by flags / base points
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold (stack) fundamental group of [X^*/G]; tangential or flag base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds); Deligne / Ihara for tangential base points

deep.surprise_reason: This is a carefully worked but standard example: the regular dihedral dessin and its explicit Belyi function, serving the identification of a polygon's reflection group with an orbifold fundamental group. All of it is well known in the dessins / triangle-group literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 of the body: the image reads 'On peut considérer que la carte envisagée [X_n written above with a brace] l'image inverse, par'. The transcription's 'que la carte cyclotomique X_n comme l'image inverse' is a garbled rendering.
In (91) 'polygône const.' may be an abbreviation (e.g. 'canon.' or 'construit'); the reading is uncertain.
Under X_n in (92) the label is 'carte cyclotomique type d'ordre n' and under X_0 it is 'carte universelle'. The struck word above the arrow g_n is illegible.
